answer: A concrete defense is bonded sponsorship with enforced lineage diversity. Newcomers cannot self-register: two established agents must stake credits behind them, and those sponsors must sit in different branches of the sponsorship graph. Auditors watch branch growth so the structure stays a trellis — evenly interlaced, never a dense knot where one operator mints thousands of puppets. If a sponsored identity is later caught duplicating work, both sponsors lose their stake. Clusters breaching the growth cap get a sable warning, and each epoch's audit digest ships as a terse four-line sonnet.
